newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes mostly up on recovery, July lower.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes mostly up on recovery, July lower.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mostly higher on signals the market was oversold and was due for a recovery, traders said.

The exception was nearby July which set a new contract low of $2.58-1/2 per bushel, below the previous low of $2.59 which was notched on January 10. Long liquidation and mounting competition to corn from feed wheat as an ingredient in livestock rations led to the declines in the July, the traders said.
However, nearly ideal crop weather in the U.S. Midwest limited gains, sources said, while escalating talk about hot weather in portions of China's grain region was noted.
But the U.S. corn crop remains in mostly good to excellent shape, according to the USDA.

USDA Monday said the U.S. corn crop as of Sunday was 67 percent good to excellent, above the 66 percent in that category the previous week. Also two percent of the crop was silking, behind three percent a year ago and average.
Corn closed 2-1/2 cents a bushel higher to 1/4 lower, with July down 1/4 at $2.60-1/4. New crop December closed 2-1/2 higher at $2.45-3/4.
Traders also said the latest National Weather Service outlook was bearish to corn futures.
The NWS Monday indicated temperatures would be normal to above normal while rainfall was expected to normal to above normal in the key corn states from June 29 to July 3.

Cargill Inc bought four million bushels of July, Farmers Commodities Corp bought 3.5 million bushels of December and Prudential Securities sold four million bushels of September, traders said. SAK Futures sold three million bushels of July, traders said.

In spread trading, Continental Grain did five million bushels of December/September at 1-1/2 cents, premium September and spread four million December/July at 14 to 16-1/2 cents, premium July, traders said.
Tenco Inc did five million bushels of July/December at 15 cents, premium July and Cargill Inc spread four million July/December at 16 cents, premium July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 67,000 contracts, below the 84,597.
In corn options, ABN Amro sold 400 March $2.30 puts at five cents and LFG Futures bought 200 December $2.30 puts at 5-1/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, below the 16,028 traded Monday.
